doc.title: Ken Peplowski interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]

chapter: Opening and the working musician's life
title: Booking tours, agents and job insecurity
summary: He books himself with agents, distrusts managers, and lives with constant job insecurity.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Do you book your own things into Spain, and those kind of tours?

It’s a combination of booking my own things, and I’ve got agents in different parts of the world. I’ve had a long lost search for a manager and it always ends in disaster. It’s very hard to find somebody that is trustworthy and that has the time to devote and that. I’ve had some experiences with managers in the past where after six months to a year you’re looking back at the year and you say well I’ve just paid this person a lot of money for things that I could have done myself. So I wind up taking everything back on again myself. It’s a lot of work though, because I can spend as much or more time on the business end as the playing end, which you really don’t want to do. But it’s a never ending search. But I do have agents in England and I have got a guy in Spain, and the record company that I’m with, Concord, sometimes people just call up the company trying to get ahold of me. So it’s kind of a combination of the phone ringing, which was © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

the case with this festival. Ralph Sutton has been a friend of mine and we’ve played together a lot so that’s the connection there. And me getting out and trying to hustle jobs. Like I’ll do mailings to colleges or orchestras, I’m doing pops concerts now and things like that.
As soon as you slack off you’re going to notice it I would imagine.

Yeah. That’s the one thing that is never, it’s not a nice thing about this business. There’s always a sense of insecurity, job insecurity. Because you may have, like we’re talking now in October, and I’m already booked into next November, a year from November. But then you start worrying about after that. Immediately. So the thing is you have to learn, again it’s a discipline and it’s always a learning lesson. You need to learn not to let that stuff get to the playing side, and not to worry about what everybody else is doing or not doing, and just try to be yourself and play the best you can. And there’s a niche for everybody.
